name: Orforglipron
summary: A GLP-1 medicine taken as a pill, sold as Foundayo, approved in April 2026 for weight management in adults with obesity or overweight with a related health problem.
what_it_is: Orforglipron is a small-molecule drug, not a peptide, that switches on the GLP-1 receptor. It lowers food intake, likely by reducing appetite, and slows stomach emptying. It is taken by mouth, and its half-life is about 29 to 49 hours. Eli Lilly has also tested it in type 2 diabetes, but so far it is approved only for weight management.

evidence.why: FDA approval for weight management based on two 72-week randomized trials in 4,740 adults, 1,613 of them with type 2 diabetes.

status_us.label: FDA-approved for weight management (April 2026)
status_us.note: Approved April 1, 2026 as Foundayo for adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one weight-related condition; it was the first new molecular entity approved under FDA's Commissioner's National Priority Voucher pilot. It is not approved for type 2 diabetes: Lilly said in June 2026 it planned to file for that use by the end of the second quarter, and no FDA decision was found.

benefits.claim: Average weight loss of about 7% to 11% over 72 weeks, depending on dose, versus about 2% with placebo, in 3,127 adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes; 60% to 72% lost at least 5% of body weight versus 27%
Average weight loss of about 5% to 10% over 72 weeks versus 2.5% with placebo in 1,613 adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight

Lower A1C in adults with type 2 diabetes: up to 2.2 points versus 1.4 with oral semaglutide over 52 weeks, and up to 1.7 versus 0.8 with dapagliflozin over 40 weeks (company-reported; not yet an approved use)

risks.risk: Nausea, constipation, diarrhea, vomiting and indigestion: nausea affected 26% to 35% versus 10% on placebo; severe digestive reactions occurred in about 3% versus 1%, and 8% stopped because of side effects versus 3%
Faster heart rate: an average rise of about 4 to 5 beats per minute, and a racing heartbeat (tachycardia) in 3% versus 0.9% on placebo
Hair loss in 4% to 5% versus 2% on placebo
Gallstones (1% versus 0.7% on placebo) and gallbladder inflammation (0.4% versus 0.3%)

Acute pancreatitis (0.14 versus 0.04 cases per 100 patient-years) and acute kidney injury (0.2% versus 0.05%); breathing stomach contents into the lungs under anesthesia or deep sedation is also a labeled warning
Boxed warning: thyroid C-cell tumors seen in rodents with GLP-1 drugs; orforglipron is not active in rats or mice and caused no tumors there, so its human relevance is undetermined

avoid_if: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN 2
Past serious allergic reaction to orforglipron
Pregnancy (the label says to stop when pregnancy is recognized) or breastfeeding (not recommended)
Type 2 diabetes with diabetic retinopathy (needs closer eye monitoring)
interactions: Birth control pills: may work less well after starting and after each dose increase; the label advises a non-oral method or an added barrier method for a time
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (such as ritonavir) or strong CYP3A4 inducers: can change orforglipron levels; the label limits or avoids some combinations
Simvastatin: orforglipron roughly doubles exposure to its active form, so the label caps the statin dose
Insulin or sulfonylureas: higher risk of low blood sugar
Other GLP-1 drugs: using them together is not recommended

before: Eye exam if you have diabetic retinopathy
during: Blood glucose if you have diabetes, especially with insulin or a sulfonylurea
Kidney function if vomiting or diarrhea is severe
Resting heart rate at regular visits
Eye checks if you have diabetic retinopathy
labs.why: The label calls for monitoring blood sugar in people with diabetes, kidney function when digestive side effects could cause dehydration, and diabetic eye disease; it reports heart-rate rises without a specific monitoring rule and says routine calcitonin or thyroid ultrasound checks are of uncertain value.

studies.title: FOUNDAYO (orforglipron) tablets, for oral use: Prescribing Information
studies.people: 3,127 adults with obesity or overweight, without diabetes (72-week placebo-controlled trial)
studies.finding: Average weight change was -7.4% to -11.1% across three doses versus -2.1% with placebo; 59.6% to 71.5% lost at least 5% of body weight versus 26.8%.

studies.title: FOUNDAYO (orforglipron) tablets, for oral use: Prescribing Information
studies.people: 1,613 adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight (72-week placebo-controlled trial)
studies.finding: Average weight change was -5.1% to -9.6% versus -2.5% with placebo; 47.4% to 67% lost at least 5% of body weight versus 26.8%.

studies.title: Lilly's oral GLP-1 Foundayo (orforglipron) delivered superior A1C control and weight loss in three pivotal type 2 diabetes trials
studies.people: Adults with type 2 diabetes in the ACHIEVE-2, ACHIEVE-3 and ACHIEVE-5 trials
studies.finding: A1C fell up to 2.2 points versus 1.4 with oral semaglutide (52 weeks) and up to 1.7 versus 0.8 with dapagliflozin (40 weeks). In those two head-to-head trials, 8.7% to 12.4% stopped because of side effects versus 1.2% to 4.9% on the comparators. Company-reported.

ask_your_clinician: Do I need to change my birth control when starting or increasing orforglipron?
Do any of my other medicines, such as statins or HIV drugs, interact with it?
Which side effects, such as severe stomach pain or a racing heart, mean I should call you?

notes_for_editor: Weight results are the label's (all randomized participants); Lilly's often-quoted 12.4% figure is for the top dose among participants who stayed on treatment (AJMC). Whether the type 2 diabetes application was filed, and its status after June 2026, were not confirmed; the July 2026 label lists weight management only, and a Drugs.com approval history (last entry June 8, 2026) showed no diabetes decision. 'Small molecule' comes from AJMC; the label gives only the chemical name. The ATTAIN and ACHIEVE papers were not opened; per Lilly, two of the three diabetes trials it reported were open-label. Prices and direct-to-consumer sales were left out on purpose.
